extracted.intended_audience: Members of the public, businesses, NGOs, and other stakeholders invited to respond to Singapore Government's NCCS consultation on climate ambition
extracted.subtask_description: A government consultation inviting views on Singapore’s proposed increase in climate ambition (net-zero by 2050), on whether to enhance the 2030 NDC, and on areas where Government, business, communities and citizens can do more. The page also summarises public feedback and outlines mitigation strategy pillars and proposed policy measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question: Is net zero by 2050 too ambitious / just right / not sufficiently ambitious?
rubrics_metrics.description: Public is asked whether net zero by 2050 is too ambitious, just right, or not sufficiently ambitious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents were also invited to propose an alternative net-zero year if they thought 2050 was not sufficiently ambitious (the consultation collected suggested alternative years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question: Should Singapore enhance its 2030 NDC?
rubrics_metrics.description: Public is asked whether Singapore should enhance its 2030 Nationally Determined Contribution, which currently pledges to peak emissions at 65 MtCO2e around 2030.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents who answered this question could indicate scope to enhance the 2030 NDC; results reported percentage agreement among respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question: In which areas is Singapore doing well and where can it do more?
rubrics_metrics.description: Public is asked to identify, across Government, businesses, communities and citizens, where Singapore is performing well in the transition and where it can do more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prompt seeks qualitative feedback across multiple actor groups to inform revisions to the LEDS and NDC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pivot away from emissions-intensive industries
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that Singapore diversify its economy and pivot away from emissions-intensive industries such as the Energy and Chemicals sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government can set concrete targets for reducing sectoral emissions or increase output of sustainable products from Jurong Island; example: Sustainable Jurong Island aspirations for sustainable products and carbon abatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Businesses to implement decarbonisation plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Businesses should put in place decarbonisation plans and commit to net-zero targets (e.g., Science Based Targets initiative) and factor ESG considerations into business models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions include incorporating a carbon cost in financial analyses, tying ESG outcomes to executive pay, encouraging employee behaviour change, reducing packaging, and pivoting to sustainable goods/services. Government can support with incentives (grants/subsidies) and disincentives; SMEs may require targeted assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage emissions reporting (including Scope 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Businesses should strengthen carbon monitoring and reporting practices for greater accountability and avoid greenwashing; consider measuring and disclosing Scope 3 emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government may consider mandatory reporting through legislation to improve accountability and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide support for workers in a green transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Government should reskill and provide support to workers affected by the green transition as part of building a workforce for the green economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support is framed as necessary alongside industry transformation to manage disruptions to business models and workers’ careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make available green financing
rubrics_metrics.description: Government and financial institutions should cease funding fossil fuel projects, divest from fossil fuels, and provide financing to businesses transitioning away from fossil fuels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes both public finance actions and incentivising private sector green financing to catalyse decarbonisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in clean energy
rubrics_metrics.description: Ramp up investment in and deployment of alternative energy technologies (for example, solar), and incentivise private home and building owners to install them; reconsider nuclear power given technological advances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The consultation references Singapore targets and measures (see energy-grid decarbonisation entry) and suggests incentives for deployment at private and public scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage green research & development (R&D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government can partner with businesses to accelerate decarbonisation by investing in R&D of novel green technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R&D support is presented as complementary to deployment and industrial transformation to bring forward viable low-carbon solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import electricity (regional low-carbon electricity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and accelerate efforts to import clean energy from regional partners (e.g., Malaysia and Laos) and develop ASEAN power grid integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electricity imports should meet Singapore’s standards/regulations and be subject to impact assessment frameworks so overseas green projects do not harm local communities or environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchase carbon credits only as a last resort
rubrics_metrics.description: Singapore should prioritise achieving absolute emission reductions first, using carbon credits as a last resort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Singapore’s development as a carbon services hub is positive, but priority must remain on domestic/actual reductions; public consultation and transparent criteria for eligible offsets are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace nature / nature-based solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritise preserving forests, mangroves and other natural habitats as nature-based solutions that contribute to carbon storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conservation and restoration are highlighted as part of a broader low-carbon approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote green commutes and electrify transport
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue to improve and electrify public transport, commit to phasing out internal combustion engine vehicles, expand EV charging infrastructure and bolster the energy grid to support EV growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures include system improvements, infrastructure roll-out, and policies to phase out ICE vehicles over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage green infrastructure and building energy-efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhance regulations to reduce building energy consumption (raise energy-efficiency requirements, set minimum air-conditioning temperatures) and consider preservation/retrofit of older buildings to avoid embodied carbon from new construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory tightening and retrofit incentives are suggested to reduce operational and embodied emissions in the built environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuals to embrace lower-carbon lifestyles
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals can reduce meat consumption, take more public transport, reduce consumption and waste, support green businesses, and participate actively in climate conversations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges that individual footprints are smaller than industry’s, but consumer behaviour shifts can signal demand and influence broader actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government to catalyse green lifestyles (education, policy levers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government can facilitate green lifestyles via strengthening local agri-food, banning single-use plastics, subsidising smart devices for household energy efficiency, incorporating sustainability into school curricula, and increasing publicity/education on climate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy, subsidies, education, and regulation are all levers to accelerate societal behavioural change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government to lead by example and continue public consultation with transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Government should continue initiatives (e.g., GreenGov.SG), lead by example, and consult the public on climate policies and plans with greater transparency on data, analyses and trade-offs considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency includes sharing data and trade-offs and ongoing public engagement to build consensus and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibrate and progressively raise the carbon tax
rubrics_metrics.description: Progressively raise the carbon tax: S$5/tCO2e (2019–2023), S$25/tCO2e (2024–2025), S$45/tCO2e (2026–2027), with a view to reaching S$50–$80/tCO2e by 2030; consider further increases and lowering the 25 ktCO2e threshold to include smaller emitters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider progressive taxation where larger emitters pay more, public disclosure of carbon tax allowances for companies, consult public and disclose criteria for determining eligible carbon credits to offset carbon tax, and provide targeted support to vulnerable households.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide support measures to households and vulnerable groups during transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Design support for households—especially vulnerable and low-income segments—so they are not adversely affected by carbon pricing and other climate policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support can be direct financial assistance, targeted subsidies, or transitional measures accompanying policy changes such as carbon tax increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement a three-part mitigation strategy: carbon tax, industry transformation, energy-grid decarbonisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigation strategy focuses on (I) implementing an effective carbon tax regime, (II) transforming industries and the economy, and (III) decarbonising the energy grid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each pillar contains concrete actions (carbon pricing schedule; Sustainable Jurong Island and industry decarbonisation measures; four 'switches' for the power system). The Government welcomes public suggestions on these pillars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transform industries and economy (Sustainable Jurong Island example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with industries to reorient sectors (e.g., Energy & Chemicals) toward sustainable production, increase sustainable product output, improve energy efficiency, deploy CCUS, and aim for large-scale carbon abatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example targets include ambitions to increase sustainable products fourfold from 2019 levels and to achieve more than six million tonnes of carbon abatement per annum in the sector by 2050; broader industry measures are referenced elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decarbonise power generation via four switches with specific targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Decarbonise the grid by: (1) deploying at least 2 GWp of solar by 2030 and 200MW/200MWh of energy storage; (2) importing up to 4 GW of low-carbon electricity by 2035; (3) deploying emerging low-carbon alternatives (CCUS, hydrogen); and (4) continuing to use natural gas in near term while scaling renewables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imports are expected to supply ~30% of electricity by 2035; trials are underway to test technical and regulatory frameworks; example import of up to 100MW from Laos noted. Planning must address intermittency and grid resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise international cooperation and ensure overseas projects meet Singapore standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Many mitigation options depend on international cooperation (e.g., renewable imports, CCUS sites, green hydrogen); Singapore should ensure overseas projects adhere to Singapore standards and conduct impact assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks should be developed for technical/regulatory aspects and to mitigate adverse effects on local communities and environments overseas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement metrics and willingness to act
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation tracks public attitudes (e.g., percent saying 2050 is not sufficiently ambitious; percent willing to make trade-offs), indicating public support for action despite potential inconveniences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metrics are used to inform policy ambition and to signal public readiness to contribute to net-zero goals.
